def Def9 (v : Form → Prop) : Prop := ¬ v fls ∧ ∀ φ ψ, v (imp φ ψ) ↔ (v φ → v ψ)
def Def10 (φ : Form) : Prop := ∀ v, Def9 v → v φ
inductive Def11 : Form → Prop
  | taut {φ : Form} : Def10 φ → Def11 φ
  | inst (x y : ℕ) (φ : Form) : Def8 y x φ → Def11 (imp (all x φ) (Def7 x y φ))
  | dist (x : ℕ) (φ ψ : Form) : Def11 (imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ)))
  | vac (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : ¬ Def6 x φ → Def11 (imp φ (all x φ))
  | k2 (φ ψ : Form) : Def11 (imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ)))
  | k3 (φ : Form) : Def11 (imp φ (K φ))
  | k4 (φ : Form) : Def11 (imp (K φ) (K (K φ)))
  | kall (x : ℕ) (φ : Form) : Def11 (imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ)))
inductive Def12 : Form → Prop
  | base {φ : Form} : Def11 φ → Def12 φ
  | gen (x : ℕ) {φ : Form} : Def12 φ → Def12 (all x φ)
def Def13 (φ : Form) : Prop := Def12 φ ∨ ∃ ψ, Def12 ψ ∧ φ = K ψ
inductive Def14 (T : Set Form) : Form → Prop
  | ax {φ : Form} : Def13 φ → Def14 T φ
  | hyp {φ : Form} : φ ∈ T → Def14 T φ
  | mp {φ ψ : Form} : Def14 T (imp φ ψ) → Def14 T φ → Def14 T ψ

translation:
Def9 is a condition on a predicate v on formulas: v does not hold of fls, and for every formula φ and every formula ψ, v holds of imp φ ψ if and only if the metalevel implication from v φ to v ψ holds. No further condition is imposed on the values of v at atoms, universally quantified formulas, or K-formulas.

Def10 holds of a formula φ if, for every predicate v on formulas, Def9 v implies v φ.

Def11 holds exactly of the formulas given by the following eight clauses. In the list, A ⇒ B denotes the object-language formula imp A B, and ∀x A denotes all x A.
1. For every formula φ, if Def10 holds of φ, include φ.
2. For every natural number x, every natural number y, and every formula φ, if Def8 y x φ holds, include (∀x φ) ⇒ (Def7 x y φ). Def7 replaces free occurrences of x in variable positions by y without renaming binders. The side condition Def8 is automatic at atoms and fls, must hold on both sides of an implication, and passes through K. At a binder ∀z θ it requires that z = x, or x is not free in θ, or both z ≠ y and the side condition holds in θ. There is no separate requirement that x and y be distinct.
3. For every x and every pair of formulas φ, ψ, include (∀x (φ ⇒ ψ)) ⇒ ((∀x φ) ⇒ (∀x ψ)).
4. For every x and every formula φ, if x is not free in φ (that is, Def6 x φ does not hold), include φ ⇒ (∀x φ).
5. For every pair of formulas φ, ψ, include K(φ ⇒ ψ) ⇒ (Kφ ⇒ Kψ).
6. For every formula φ, include φ ⇒ Kφ, in that direction.
7. For every formula φ, include Kφ ⇒ K(Kφ).
8. For every x and every formula φ, include K(∀x φ) ⇒ (∀x Kφ).

Def12 is the least property containing every Def11 formula and closed under universal prefixing: for every natural number x and every formula φ, if Def12 holds of φ, it holds of ∀x φ. Thus a Def12 formula is a Def11 formula with zero or more universal quantifiers prefixed, with no side condition on the variables.

Def13 holds of a formula φ if and only if either Def12 holds of φ, or there exists a formula ψ such that Def12 holds of ψ and φ is exactly Kψ. The second alternative adds one outer K to a Def12 formula; it is not a rule recursively applied to Def13 formulas.

Def14 fixes any set T of formulas and defines derivability for that T. It is the least property of formulas with these rules: for every φ, if Def13 holds of φ, then φ is derivable; for every φ, if φ belongs to T, then φ is derivable; and for every φ and ψ, if φ ⇒ ψ is derivable from T and φ is derivable from that same T, then ψ is derivable from T. No condition is imposed on T. Modus ponens is the only rule combining derivations; there is no separate Def14 rule prefixing a universal quantifier or K to an arbitrary derived formula.

divergences.description: Reinhardt’s factivity axiom is `K φ → φ`, but `Def11.k3` asserts its converse, `φ → K φ`. The latter lets one infer `K φ` even when `φ` is merely a hypothesis in `T`. The passage’s discussion of the rule `p / Bp` does not justify this object-language implication or supply the missing factivity axiom.

`Def12` allows any universal prefix, including one that leaves variables free or binds variables vacuously. Thus `Def13` also admits `K ψ` when `ψ` is still open, whereas Reinhardt specifies universal closures and speaks of prefixing `B` to the resulting sentences.
`Def14.hyp` accepts open formulas as premises. Reinhardt defines deduction from a set `T` of sentences; Lean includes that case but does not restrict `T` to it.

As declared in the claim, the relational fragment has only variables as terms, so instantiation is variable-for-variable. It cannot state the cited equality axiom (Leibniz’s law) or the arithmetic schemas, including induction in the expanded language.

judgement.summary: Within the declared fragment, Lean captures modus ponens and three of Reinhardt’s four special axioms. Reversing factivity changes the proof system materially, independently of the broader treatment of open formulas.
